A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TopoCellGen work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation results on BRCA-M2C and Lizard, downstream detection/classification experiments, and loss-component, loss-weight, and learning-rate ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a pathologist assessment and spatial point-pattern comparisons in supplementary Sections 14–15.

M1.justification: The count-conditioned diffusion model, counting loss, intra-class and inter-class topological losses, training objective, inference procedure, and layout-conditioned image generator are unchanged. Revised illustrations and additional implementation explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use BRCA-M2C and Lizard for cell-layout generation, with layout-guided image synthesis and downstream detection/classification augmentation. The new expert and spatial analyses assess existing generated layouts without introducing another dataset, tissue domain, cell population, or input condition.

E2.justification: ADM, TMCCG, and Spatial Diffusion remain the generation comparators and are reused in the new spatial analysis. Table 2 retains the same augmentation comparisons for UNet and MCSpatNet. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds protocols for one pathologist to assess 10 randomly selected real/synthetic pairs without type labels, and for comparing three intra-class K-functions and six cross-K-functions at six radii. Existing training budgets, splits, preprocessing, and downstream evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary Sections 14–15 substantially broaden validation of biological realism through expert assessment of authenticity and tissue characteristics, plus conventional spatial analysis of intra-class clustering and inter-class interactions. The existing ablations and cell-count distribution analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The new spatial analysis specifies paired t-tests across 54 radius/type combinations and reports counts with p > 0.05 in Tables 6–7. Table 2's uncertainty values and significance highlighting are unchanged; no additional repeated-run counts or seed information are disclosed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figure 7's distributions are unchanged. v2 adds the expert's 60% synthetic-layout identification accuracy and reported preservation of tissue characteristics. Tables 6–7 report 12/18 intra-class and 24/36 inter-class non-significant comparisons for TopoCellGen, versus 2/18 and 10/36 for ADM, 5/18 and 17/36 for TMCCG, and 6/18 and 15/36 for Spatial Diffusion.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, loss definitions, Wasserstein matching, TopoFD construction, and supplementary persistent-homology and MMD formulations are unchanged. The new spatial tests introduce empirical procedures, without new mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: topology-aware cell-layout diffusion, the counting loss, and TopoFD, together with improved synthetic layouts and downstream performance. The shortened conclusion preserves these scientific claims rather than redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the expert assessment as evidence of realism and preserved benign/malignant characteristics, and the K-function tests as evidence of closer spatial agreement. It also adds a data-parallel scalability assertion. The limitations concerning unseen cell types and 256-by-256 patches remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, clarifies that the reported FID uses Spatial Diffusion's autoencoder-based spatial-FID with a separately trained Lizard autoencoder, and reports training within 200 hours. The GPU, batch sizes, training steps, and principal hyperparameters were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds InverseSR and Mine Your Own Anatomy, replaces the CellDETR reference with Prangemeier et al.'s transformer-based cell segmentation paper, and explicitly attributes spatial-FID to Spatial Diffusion. The broader positioning against existing layout-generation and topology-aware methods is retained.

P1.justification: Results prose and the conclusion are condensed, contact information and acknowledgments are updated, and the supplementary roadmap accommodates three new sections. Most wording and section organization remain intact; the existing limitations move from Section 14 to Section 17.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 8 and Tables 6–7, updates cell-type legends and colors in existing illustrations, relocates unchanged Figures 6–7, and adjusts spacing around tables and text. The overall two-column layout and existing table structures remain similar.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through the spatial-FID clarification, code pointer, and runtime disclosure, while adding complementary biological and spatial validation absent from v1. The evidential gain is limited: the expert study involves one pathologist and 10 pairs, and counting non-significant tests does not establish spatial equivalence. These additions support a modest overall improvement despite overconfident interpretations of the new validation.
